The '''2020 Copa del Rey final''' was a football match that decided the winner of the [[2019–20 Copa del Rey]], the 118th edition of Spain's [[Copa del Rey|primary football cup]] (including two seasons where two rival editions were played). The match was played at the [[Estadio de La Cartuja]] in [[Seville]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/02/05/football/1580911629_748235.html|title=Official: La Cartuja stadium in Seville to host Copa del Rey finals until 2023|website=as.com|publisher=AS|date=5 February 2020|access-date=5 March 2020|archive-date=12 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210412184505/https://en.as.com/en/2020/02/05/football/1580911629_748235.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> between [[Athletic Bilbao]] and [[Real Sociedad]], the first [[Basque derby]] final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://es.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea033518e97-56eaf20965ce-1000--un-derbi-vasco-en-la-final/|title=Copa del Rey: El Athletic asegura un derbi en la final|trans-title=Copa del Rey: Athletic ensures a derby in the final |website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|language=es|date=5 March 2020|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2021/apr/02/copa-del-rey-final-real-sociedad-athletic-bilbao-basque-derby|title=A final like no other: la Real, Athletic and the biggest Basque derby ever|first=Sid|last=Lowe|work=The Guardian|date=2 April 2021|access-date=2 April 2021}}</ref> 

Originally scheduled for 18 April 2020, the match was postponed with the agreement of the participating clubs on 11 March (with no new date decided at that point) due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]], which had led to football matches being cancelled or played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] as a measure to prevent the spread of the virus, in the hope that the delay would provide time to contain the outbreak and allow the final to take place with a full stadium as in normal circumstances.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2020/03/11/aplazada-la-final-de-la-copa-del-rey|title=The final of the Copa del Rey postponed|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=11 March 2020|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref> The final was played on 3 April 2021,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2021/01/28/official-the-copa-del-rey-2019-20-final-set-for-april-3/|title=Official: The Copa del Rey 2019-20 final set for April 3|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=28 January 2021|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref> despite earlier press rumours that had suggested it would be a day later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2020/11/15/5fb153c146163f0a868b4622.html|title=Last season's Copa del Rey final to be on April 4 and this year's on April 18|date=15 November 2020|access-date=15 November 2020|newspaper=Marca}}</ref>

Real Sociedad won the final 1–0 thanks to a second-half [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] converted by [[Mikel Oyarzabal]], achieving their second Copa del Rey title<ref>{{cite web |url=https://rfef.es/en/noticias/track-record-the-team-in-white-win-their-20th-copa-trophy |title=TRACK RECORD - The team in white win their 20th Copa trophy. - LIST OF WINNERS OF THE SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP - COPA DE SM EL REY |website=RFEF.es (RFEF official website) |date=7 May 2023 |access-date=10 May 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230507224626/https://rfef.es/en/noticias/track-record-the-team-in-white-win-their-20th-copa-trophy |archive-date=7 May 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/conferencia/REVISTA%20RFEF%20141%20OK.pdf#70|title=Historial|access-date=10 May 2023|author=Real Federación Española de Fútbol|date=March 2011|magazine=Revista Oficial de la R.F.E.F.|page=70|format=pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120718164817/http://www.rfef.es/FCKeditor/UserFiles/File/conferencia/REVISTA%20RFEF%20141%20OK.pdf|archive-date=18 July 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> (in [[1909 Copa del Rey|1909]] it was won by its forerunner, [[Club Ciclista de San Sebastián]]), ending a 34-year trophy drought dating to [[1987 Copa del Rey Final|1987]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56627359|title=Oyarzabal scores winner in Copa del Rey final|website=BBC Sport|date=3 April 2021|access-date=3 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/03/athletic-bilbao-real-sociedad-copa-del-rey-2020-final-match-report |title=Real Sociedad beat Athletic to claim Copa del Rey and Basque glory|first=Sid|last=Lowe|work=The Guardian|date=3 April 2021|access-date=3 April 2021}}</ref>

==Background==
Real Sociedad were competing in their eighth Copa del Rey final, having lost their last final in [[1988 Copa del Rey Final|1988]] to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]. Athletic Bilbao were competing in their 38th final,{{efn|Athletic's website claimed it was their 40th final,<ref name="16th"/> but this total included the [[1902 Copa de la Coronación]], the status of which is disputed both as a Copa del Rey event and as a tournament entered by their club, and the scheduled [[1904 Copa del Rey]] final which was never played.}} having lost their last final in [[2015 Copa del Rey final|2015]], also to Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |last=Tejedor Carnicero |first=José Vicente |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancuphist.html |title=Spain – List of Cup Finals |website=RSSSF |publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |date=18 July 2019 |access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref> In reaching the final, both teams were assured qualification for the four-team [[2021 Supercopa de España]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51766095|title=Copa del Rey: Athletic Bilbao beat Granada to set up all-Basque final with Sociedad|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 March 2020|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref>{{efn|As the result of the match was not known before the start of the 2021 Supercopa, both teams qualified.}} this four-team competition was played in January 2021 and won by Athletic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/barcelona-vs-athletic/cronica/2021/01/17/6004bcd422601d7c438b4632.html|title=Williams sinks Barcelona and Athletic claim the Supercopa|newspaper=Marca|first=Arch|last=Bell|date=17 January 2021|access-date=1 February 2021}}</ref>

In the [[1910 Copa del Rey]] (which had two rival tournaments running in parallel), the two clubs participated in the three-team group of the UECF competition along with [[Real Madrid CF|Madrid FC]]. The [[1910 UECF Copa del Rey Final|decisive match]] was between the Basque teams (Athletic winning 1–0),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euskonews.com/0290zbk/gaia29002es.html|title=El Athletic de Bilbao, campeón de la Copa de España de fútbol de 1910|date=25 February 2005 |trans-title=Athletic de Bilbao, champion of the 1910 Spanish Cup|language=es|publisher=Euskonews & Media|access-date=6 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/03/05/athletic-bilbao-granada-copa-del-rey-all-basque-final|title=Athletic Bilbao Scores Late to Set Up All-Basque Copa Del Rey Final|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=6 March 2020|access-date=6 March 2020}}</ref> but as it was not a final in the traditional [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout format]] and the newly-formed Real Sociedad were playing under the name 'Vasconia' for licensing reasons,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa10.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030910160228/http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa10.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=10 September 2003|title=Copa del Rey Alfonso XIII 1910|website=LinguaSport|language=es}}</ref> it was not widely recognised as an equivalent to their meeting 110 years later.<ref name="16th">{{cite news|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2021/03/23/real-sociedad-our-16th-different-copa-final-opponent/|title=Real Sociedad, our 16th different Copa final opponent|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=23 March 2021|access-date=23 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/es/noticias/detalle/derbi-final|title=Será un derbi|trans-title=It will be a derby|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=5 March 2020|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref>

===350-day delay===
Around the time of the original date for the final, the Spanish football federation ([[RFEF]]) had indicated they would grant the designated [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League group stage|Europa League group stage]] berth, typically given to the winners of the tournament, to Athletic Bilbao ([[2019–20 La Liga|10th position in La Liga]] at the time of its suspension with eleven rounds remaining) should the match not be played within the period of 2019–20,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/04/30/football/1588282918_920167.html|title=Ibai Gomez: 'I prefer to play the Copa del Rey with fans than qualify for Europe|website=Football España|date=2 May 2020|access-date=5 March 2020|archive-date=2 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502022948/https://en.as.com/en/2020/04/30/football/1588282918_920167.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> as Real Sociedad (4th place) seemed likely to qualify for at least the Europa League and possibly the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] via their league position. However, on 30 April, [[UEFA]] stated that the final must be played by 3 August to activate the designated qualification place, otherwise this would revert to the team finishing seventh in La Liga (either with the fixtures completed or the standings declared).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/04/30/football/1588282918_920167.html|title=The team that finishes 7th will play the Europa League if there is no Copa del Rey final|newspaper=Diario AS|date=30 April 2020|access-date=5 March 2020|archive-date=2 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502022948/https://en.as.com/en/2020/04/30/football/1588282918_920167.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]], it would be very unlikely that any final played by then would allow spectators into the stadium, a factor both clubs had declared was essential when it was initially postponed. Athletic submitted a formal protest against UEFA's instruction,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2020/05/01/comunicado-oficial-2|title=Official announcement|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=1 May 2020|access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> and on 4 May both teams officially reiterated their stance to delay the match until such a time as supporters would be able to attend it.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2020/05/04/comunicado-oficial-3|title=Official announcement|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=4 May 2020|access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/en/news/details/official-announcement-2|title=Copa del Rey{{!}}Official announcement|publisher=Real Sociedad|date=4 May 2020|access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref>

When the league resumed in June 2020, the form of both clubs was poor: Athletic Bilbao [[2019–20 Athletic Bilbao season|collected 14 points]] from 33 available, while Real Sociedad [[2019–20 Real Sociedad season|gained only 10 points]] and slipped down the table; however, five of those came in the last three matchdays, including one from an 88th-minute equaliser against [[Atlético Madrid]] on the final day<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/match/atl%C3%A9tico-madrid-v-real-sociedad/report/i9wb7xs5sstwhbe61futw7e2|title=Atletico Madrid 1-1 Real Sociedad: Late Januzaj equaliser secures Europa League spot|website=Goal.com|date=19 July 2020|access-date=19 July 2020}}</ref> to keep them just above [[Granada C.F.|Granada]] and [[Getafe C.F.|Getafe]] – they finished sixth and qualified for the Europa League group stage, the same status as would have been afforded the Copa winner. Athletic's challenge had already fallen short and they placed eleventh.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://insideathletic.com/2020/07/16/athletic-club-0-2-leganes-the-race-for-europe-ends/|title=Athletic Club 0-2 Leganés: The Race For Europe Ends|website=Inside Athletic|date=16 July 2020|access-date=19 July 2020}}</ref>

==Route to the final==
{{details|2019–20 Copa del Rey}}
Real Sociedad played in eight matches in the competition (including the final), winning each of them without needing extra time or penalties to progress on any occasion, the run including a dramatic away victory over [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] at the quarter-final stage.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/feb/06/real-madrid-sociedad-copa-del-rey-match-report|title=Real Madrid dumped out by Real Sociedad in Copa del Rey thriller|first=Sid|last=Lowe|work=The Guardian|date=6 February 2020|access-date=6 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51407347|title=Real Madrid 3–4 Real Sociedad|website=BBC Sport|date=6 February 2020|access-date=6 April 2021}}</ref> By contrast, Athletic required a [[penalty shootout]] to eliminate two lower-division opponents and only defeated [[Granada CF|Granada]] on the [[away goals rule]] in the semi-finals;<ref>{{cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/03/05/soccer/1583437379_278679.html|title=Yuri breaks Granada's hearts to set up all-Basque final|newspaper=Diario AS|date=5 March 2020|access-date=11 April 2024}}</ref> however, they did eliminate the title holders [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] who had at least reached the final in the previous six editions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51407354|title=Athletic Bilbao 1–0 Barcelona|website=BBC Sport|date=6 February 2020|access-date=11 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/cronica/2020/02/06/5e3c8e6d46163f9b898b4620.html|title=Barcelona fall to Athletic at the death|newspaper=Marca|location=Madrid|first=Arch|last=Bell|date=6 February 2020|access-date=11 April 2024}}</ref>
